title: Vault encryption envelope: AES-256-GCM with authenticated header
description: Spec §6.3. Pure module: 32-byte key, fresh 12-byte nonce, 16-byte tag, AAD binding domain/formatVersion/vaultId/revision. Authenticate before decode; reject unknown formats, bad lengths, oversized input.

acceptanceCriteria.text: T03: known-answer or independently cross-checked AES-GCM vectors, round-trip, nonce sampling, wrong-key and malformed-length tests pass
T04: flipping any byte of ciphertext, nonce, tag, or authenticated header fails before decoded data is used

implementationNotes: Delivered in PR #10: src/domain/envelope.ts, five vault_* catalogue codes (validation, exit 6), and a new domain layer. The AAD is the UTF-8 encoding of ["opum.ward.vault", 1, vaultId, revision], with the vault ID required to be canonical lowercase UUIDv4 and the revision a safe integer of at least 1. T03 evidence: McGrew-Viega GCM cases 13-16, run through node:crypto in both directions, match under Bun (BoringSSL) and Node 24.20 (OpenSSL 3.5.7). A golden envelope record, recorded identically under both runtimes, pins the AAD encoding. Also a round trip from 0 B to the 10 MiB limit, 10,000-sample nonce distinctness plus bit balance, a wrong key, and malformed lengths and headers. T04 evidence: every byte of ciphertext, nonce and tag flipped under two masks, truncated and extended ciphertext, and every vault-ID character and the revision relabelled; each fails with vault_authentication_failed. Independent review (opum-workflow reviewer) found nothing at critical, high or medium, and six lows, all fixed here. L1: every byte input is copied once through the TypedArray constructor, and header fields are read once into a fresh object. Measured before the fix: a subclass overriding length bypassed the 10 MiB limit, and getters changed the AAD. L2: the caller-supplied-nonce primitive is no longer exported. L3: seal builds the record field by field, so extra header properties are not persisted and formatVersion cannot be overridden. L4: tests added for string plaintext, liar lengths, a header read exactly once, a SharedArrayBuffer key, and the index-19 vault-ID case. L5: null or fake inputs raise catalogue codes, not TypeErrors. L6: the OpenSSL version is corrected. Zeroing of unverified bytes on authentication failure remains best effort and untested; the module comment says so. Planted regressions, each reverted afterwards: skipped final() fails 14 tests; AAD without the revision, 5; fixed nonce, 3; no nonce-length check, 5; no open size limit, 1; trusting the caller's view, 3; spreading the header into the record, 1; no plaintext type check, 3. Not enforced here, owned by the storage and secret layers: the 64 KiB per-value limit, the revision increment, and header-only persistence. Rollback is not detected, which is a stated limit.
finalSummary: Added the vault encryption envelope (spec §6.3) as a pure domain module. AES-256-GCM under a 32-byte key, a fresh random 12-byte nonce on every seal, a 16-byte tag, and the header (domain, format version, vault ID, revision) bound as authenticated data. open() copies and validates every input and authenticates before it returns anything. Failures use fixed catalogue codes. T03 and T04 are covered by test/envelope.test.ts: published GCM vectors in both directions under Bun, reproduced by Node's OpenSSL; a golden format record; limits; nonce sampling; and byte flips across ciphertext, nonce, tag and header. Eight planted regressions each fail the suite. Independent review found no critical, high or medium issues, and its six lows are fixed. bun run check passes 129/129. Evidence is PR #10 and its CI run.
